causes.remedy: Seal or replace the leaking joints, hoses and couplings, then repeat the pressure-hold test with the unit stopped and the plant isolated. Leaks return, so add a walk-round listening check to the routine in task 7.3.2 rather than treating this as a one-off repair.

causes.remedy: Fit a new purge valve kit and check the silencer for erosion while the valve is out. Refit, run a full regeneration cycle and confirm that the purge pressure returns to its resting value between changeovers and that the unit reaches its cut-out point again. A valve that has leaked for a long time usually means the silencer packing is damaged too; replace both together.

Run a full regeneration cycle and confirm that the purge pressure falls back promptly and that the discharge noise is back to its usual level. Check the purge valve at the same time, because packing debris often damages the seat.

causes.remedy: Replace the desiccant charge in both towers and clean the tower screens while they are open. Put the cause of the overload right at the same time: a blocked separator drain, a warm intake or a missed regeneration will exhaust the new charge just as fast. Record the change so the next inspection interval starts from the correct date.

causes.remedy: No repair is needed on the unit. Reduce the demand, move the heaviest consumers out of the peak, or plan additional compressed-air capacity. causes.remedy: No repair is needed on the unit. Improve the ventilation of the room, duct the warm outlet air away from the intake, or move the heat source. Until the room is put right, monitor the oil temperature and the difference between it and the ambient reading: as long as that difference stays normal, the cooling circuit is sound. Watch the delivered air for moisture as well, because a warm intake loads the dryer more heavily.

causes.remedy: No repair is needed on the unit. Keep the room above the lower operating limit, close the source of the cold draught, or fit room heating. Until then, monitor the oil temperature during the warm-up after each start and drain condensate from the vessel more often, because water separates out of oil that never gets warm. Report repeated hard starts, since they shorten the life of the motor.

The tower indication on the display stops alternating and the air leaving the dryer becomes wet in the hours that follow.
